import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Identify potential drivers using t-statistics
    t_stats = np.array([abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(fid)], 
                                           feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(fid)])[0]) 
                       for fid in feats.ids])
    
    # Find top features by t-statistic
    top_indices = np.argsort(t_stats)[::-1][:20]
    top_ids = [feats.ids[i] for i in top_indices]
    
    # Check for correlated pairs and remove near-duplicates
    corr_pairs = []
    for i in range(len(top_ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(top_ids)):
            fid1, fid2 = top_ids[i], top_ids[j]
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid1)], 
                              feats.x[:, feats.column(fid2)])[0,1]) >= 0.6:
                corr_pairs.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Remove one feature from each correlated pair (keep higher t-stat)
    selected_ids = set()
    for fid1, fid2 in corr_pairs:
        t1, t2 = t_stats[feats.ids.index(fid1)], t_stats[feats.ids.index(fid2)]
        if t1 > t2:
            selected_ids.add(fid1)
        else:
            selected_ids.add(fid2)
    
    # Add remaining top features not in correlated pairs
    for fid in top_ids:
        if fid not in selected_ids:
            selected_ids.add(fid)
    
    # Select final drivers (highest t-stats among selected)
    final_drivers = sorted(list(selected_ids), key=lambda x: t_stats[feats.ids.index(x)], reverse=True)
    final_drivers = final_drivers[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # Cluster features to find modules
    if len(final_drivers) > 1:
        driver_indices = [feats.column(fid) for fid in final_drivers]
        driver_data = feats.x[:, driver_indices]
        
        # Use hierarchical clustering to group correlated features
        similarity_matrix = cosine_similarity(driver_data)
        clustering = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=1, linkage='average')
        cluster_labels = clustering.fit_predict(1 - similarity_matrix)
        
        # If we have a coherent module, use all features in it
        if len(set(cluster_labels)) == 1:
            columns = tuple(final_drivers)
            # Create products between all pairs in the module
            products = [(a, b) for i, a in enumerate(columns) for b in columns[i+1:]]
            # Create loadings for weighted score
            loadings = dict(zip(columns, np.ones(len(columns))))
            return Design(drivers=tuple(final_drivers), columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
    
    # Default case: use top features without interaction terms
    return Design(drivers=tuple(final_drivers), columns=tuple(final_drivers), products=(), loadings={})
